title: StringBuilder and StringBuffer in practical Java code
answer: Yes. Both `StringBuilder` and `StringBuffer` are mutable character-sequence classes with similar APIs such as `append`, `insert`, `delete`, and `reverse`. `StringBuilder` is not synchronized and is usually preferred for local, single-threaded construction because it avoids synchronization overhead. `StringBuffer` synchronizes its methods and can be useful when the same mutable buffer truly needs coordinated access across threads, although higher-level concurrency designs are often better. AeroTopo uses `StringBuilder` for repeated local construction in `expandRuns` and for efficient reversal.
